title: Password Sharing Exposure
briefing: An internal audit reveals that several employees have been sharing login credentials to access restricted systems. The security team must determine whether this behavior has created a meaningful security risk and how to respond.

injects.title: Additional Shared Accounts Found
injects.message: Further review of access logs reveals that several additional employees may have shared credentials.

injects.title: Management Response
injects.message: Managers state that password sharing occurred because system access procedures were slow and inconvenient.

injects.title: Compliance Attention
injects.message: Compliance officers note that shared credentials may violate internal security policy and regulatory requirements.

injects.title: Security Awareness Request
injects.message: Leadership asks whether security awareness training should address credential sharing risks.

step_1.situation: An audit identifies several employees sharing login credentials to access restricted applications.

if_correct.consequence: The team identifies the primary risks associated with credential sharing and begins assessing the exposure.

if_incorrect.consequence: Credential sharing is treated as a minor issue, delaying further investigation.

step_1.situation: Security reviews authentication logs and identity management policies to understand how widely credentials may have been shared.

if_correct.consequence: Review of identity and access data improves visibility into how the shared credentials were used.

if_incorrect.consequence: Failure to analyze identity logs leaves uncertainty about the scale of the issue.

step_1.situation: Management asks whether the credential sharing should be treated as a formal security incident or a policy violation.

if_correct.consequence: The team provides a balanced response explaining the risks while avoiding unnecessary escalation.

if_incorrect.consequence: Unclear communication causes confusion between security, management, and compliance teams.

step_1.situation: Security evaluates whether stronger authentication controls could reduce the likelihood of credential sharing.

if_correct.consequence: Improved authentication practices reduce the need for credential sharing.

if_incorrect.consequence: Weak authentication controls continue to encourage credential sharing behavior.

step_1.situation: Security teams consider how to reinforce credential security policies across the organization.

if_correct.consequence: Security awareness and policy communication strengthen identity security practices.

if_incorrect.consequence: Poor communication allows unsafe credential practices to continue.
